dek: A Las Vegas betting personality who sells picks on WagerTalk and was known on Pregame as Vegas-Runner. His Steam Sheet was on sale for $5 when we checked. The guarantee pays in site credit, the records are seller picked streaks, and older forum posts carry serious, unproven allegations.

short_answer: Gianni the Greek is a real, long running name in Las Vegas betting media. A 2018 WagerTalk press release names him as Gianni Karalis and says he started as a bookmaker in Philadelphia in the late 1980s and later worked as a runner at the Stardust. His WagerTalk page was active on 17 Nov 2026 with dated plays and packages for sale.

Whether the picks make money over time is not shown anywhere we could open. The page lists streaks such as "STEAM-SHEET = "48-21" (70%) on L/69 OVERALL" and "FINSHED #1 CFB AND NFL/CFB PROFIT LY", all chosen and graded by the selling site. No full log of every pick was available.

Under the name Vegas-Runner he drew strong criticism on forums between 2009 and 2011, including claims of losing runs, renamed packages and alias accounts. Those are allegations by anonymous posters that we could not verify, and a few members defended him. Treat him as a known media name with an unproven pick record.
pricing_intro: All prices below were on the Gianni the Greek WagerTalk page on 17 Nov 2026. WagerTalk shows a higher list price next to most sale prices; we give both. The All Access passes on the page are WagerTalk passes, and the page does not say they cover only his picks.

guarantee: The guarantee is an extra you pay for. The $5.00 Steam Sheet costs $8.00 with it. WagerTalk says the option "backs your purchase with 100% in credits" and applies "If your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays." The paid amount comes back as account credit for a future purchase, not as cash.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold “as is”" and that no refund is issued once a product has been purchased, delivered or viewed. The site terms add that the buyer's exclusive remedy is a refund of the price paid or replacement of the product, at WagerTalk's option. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: The media claims are real in the sense that the press release lists them: a CNBC sports betting special, a New York Times Magazine piece, the documentary "The Best of It" and radio appearances. Media exposure shows he is well known. It is not evidence that his picks win.

Every streak on the page starts where the seller chose. The hot streak block was last updated on 13 Nov, before the newest plays on the page. A forum member who reposted one of his plays on TheRX in late Oct 2026 listed his 2026 college football record as 23-24, which is a reminder that the full picture can look very different from a streak.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick with the line and release time, and no third party audit.

What the seller publishes: streak totals, a leaderboard and a Last 20 table of recent plays. On 17 Nov 2026 we counted 13 wins and 7 losses in that table. WagerTalk grades these itself and also sells the picks.
Older claims about his record come from forum posters in 2009 to 2011, who said his paid plays on Pregame lost heavily in some seasons. We could not check those figures either.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Gianni the Greek pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Gianni the Greek performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his page run from about 65% to 92% winners. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Most independent comment on this seller is old and was written about Vegas-Runner, his name on Pregame. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found about a dozen independent posts, almost all from 2009 to 2011 and about Vegas-Runner, his name on Pregame, on TheRX, Sportsbook Review and ComplaintsBoard. The repeated themes are claims of losing seasons on paid plays, packages renamed after bad runs, praise from alias accounts and critical posts removed. Against that, a few members said they won following him, that he bets his own money on fights and that his free videos were very good. Since he joined WagerTalk in 2018 we found reposted plays and one 2022 Reddit thread where a bettor reported success on his MMA picks while doubting the posted records. None of the older claims was ever proven.

A TheRX thread titled as an expose of Vegas-Runner alleged a long list of problems: an investment style betting fund in 2004 that the poster said lost client money, a losing package renamed after a bad month in 2008, posted records the poster said were better than the real results, and many alias accounts. Five replies agreed and one asked for hard evidence. None of it is proven, and no reply came from the seller.

On a ComplaintsBoard page about Pregame, one buyer said he paid for a week of Vegas-Runner picks and had six losing days out of seven. He also said the members praising Vegas-Runner were probably the same person under other names, which we could not check.
On the same page another commenter defended Vegas-Runner, saying he had followed the picks for years with good results and that the accusations came without proof.
A later commenter on that page claimed Vegas-Runner had lost over 100 units for his clients that year and said the TV networks that interviewed him never checked his record. No log was attached.

In an SBR thread about Pregame, one member said Vegas-Runner's free information was useful but that he would not buy picks from someone who was losing and, in his view, not honest about it. Other members replied that Vegas-Runner bets his own money on fights and that his free fight videos and market notes were very good.

A TheRX member claimed a Pregame handicapper persona was not a real person and accused Vegas-Runner of writing stories that built that persona up. This is one poster's claim with no evidence attached.

On Reddit, a bettor asked whether anyone subscribed to him and said he had been very strong at MMA and baseball that season. One reply said they had a lot of success following his MMA picks but did not know how much his posted records were manipulated. Another said a big parlay shown on a broadcast was props that had already hit, not plays he picked in advance.
In a TheRX service play thread, members reposted Gianni the Greek college football plays. One listed his 2026 college football record as 23-24 next to the pick. We could not confirm that figure.

Our Reddit archive searches for Gianni the Greek and Vegas-Runner in four betting subreddits found only the 2022 thread above; the full text search of r/sportsbook timed out. We found no Better Business Bureau, court or regulator record naming him.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks, grades his record, writes his bio and published the 2018 press release about him. None of those numbers is independent of the seller.

Pregame, where he sold as Vegas-Runner, also ran the forum where much of the old praise and criticism appeared. Posters on ComplaintsBoard and TheRX alleged that critical posts were removed and that some praise came from alias accounts. We could not verify either claim.
TheRX lists "All Wagertalk Cappers" among the services members may not post in its daily service play threads. The rule does not say why, and it says nothing about the quality of the picks.
strengths: A named person with a long, public career in Las Vegas betting media.
Sold through a marketplace with a named Las Vegas seller address, written terms and a refund policy.
Low entry price: the Steam Sheet was $5.00 on 17 Nov 2026, and the page shows recent losses as well as wins.
concerns: No full public record. Every headline number is a streak chosen and graded by the seller.
The guarantee costs extra and pays in site credit, never cash. All sales are final.
Serious allegations from 2009 to 2011 forum posters about losses, renamed packages and alias accounts, never tested in any court or regulator record we found.
Claims such as "a mathematical certainty" of long term winning cannot be true for any betting product.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, well known Las Vegas betting personality who sells picks through WagerTalk, which has written terms and a Las Vegas address. We could not verify that his picks win over time. Forum posters from 2009 to 2011 made serious allegations about his Pregame era, which we could not verify, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Gianni the Greek cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 his Steam Sheet was $5.00 ($8.00 with the guarantee), short sport passes were $49.00, and a one year pass was $1188.00. WagerTalk all access passes ran from $39.00 for a day to $1,999.00 for a year.
Does Gianni the Greek have a verified record?
No. The page shows streaks such as 48-21 on the Steam Sheet, graded by WagerTalk. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.
Is Gianni the Greek the same person as Vegas-Runner?
Yes, according to his own WagerTalk bio, which says he is known as Ace, Vegas-Runner and Gianni the Greek. Most of the older forum discussion about him uses the Vegas-Runner name.
